elements.name: Admirals Lord Horatio Nelson and Sir George Murray

osmTags.inscription: This was the site of The Central Junior Girls' C of E School, 1884‒1968, founded in 1812 as The Sussex Central School for Girls
The poet, Cathedral sexton and much respected Cicestrian Charles Crocker, 1797‒1861, died in this house, 6 October 1861
This twitten led to Halsted & Sons' Ironfoundry c.1840‒1932 (now Baffins Lane Car Park). C. T. Halsted was twice Mayor of this City
From 1787 to 1828 this building was the home of John Marsh, composer, musician, diarist and writer. A prominent and charitable citizen of Chichester.
Ethel Margaret ‘Madge’ Turner, 1884‒1948, Chichester’s most prominent campaigner for women’s suffrage, studied here at The Technical Institute and School of Art, 1900.

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
